conviction_note: The headline is already out: on 16 Oct Lufax pre-announced a Q3 net loss of RMB1.3-1.7bn. What the print adds is the breakdown (how much is credit impairment and how much is non-cash tax), the Q3 asset-quality numbers and the first call with the new CFO. On the one confirmed print in the last year (Q2, 18 Aug amc) the ADS fell 5.2% the next day, and the stock is down 33% in 20 days at roughly 0.05x book. So p_up is 46, a slight lean negative because the operating loss was attributed to higher credit impairment, against an abs_move of 7 for a thin ADS with 63% realised vol. Findings sum to -0.5, close to the scaled -0.56; the two agree because nothing found here is both decisive and unpriced.
bar: The company's own pre-announcement: Q3 2026 net loss of RMB1,300m-1,700m (midpoint 1,500m) against an H1 2026 net loss of RMB694m. Profit warning, HKEX announcement filed as Ex. 99.1 to the 6-K of 2026-10-16: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1816007/000119312526423425/d180390dex991.htm. There is no usable sell-side EPS bar. MarketBeat shows a +$1.08 EPS consensus, which is clearly an error for a pre-announced loss (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-lufax-lu-set-to-post-earnings-on-tuesday-2026-10-23/). Earnings Whispers says there is no usable EPS consensus (https://www.earningswhispers.com/epsdetails/LU). A HK-dollar average price target was cut 34% to HK$7.72 on 2026-10-22 (via the MarketBeat page), so analysts have moved after the warning. print_vs_bar_pct is 0: I expect the net loss inside the guided range.
positioning_check: Short interest 6.51% of float, days to cover 2.59, up 6.43% month on month (MarketBeat LU page, updated 2026-10-27: https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/lufax-nyselu-stock-price-up-86-after-analyst-upgrade-2026-07-28/). That is not a crowded short. Benzinga shows an older 2.3% short float. No skew: the Yahoo chain is unusable (ATM legs not two-sided, strikes apparently not adjusted for the 1-for-10 ADS ratio change effective about 2026-10-23); put/call OI ratio 4.92 on only 438 contracts total. Tape (split-adjusted Yahoo): $8.31, -32.98% over 20 days, -74.9% from the 52-week high, 3.1% above the 52-week low, 20-day realised vol 63%, about 206k ADS a day (~$1.7m turnover). Ping An owns 73.3% fully diluted (13D/A, 2026-08-28), so the free float is small.

findings.finding: The 16 Oct profit warning blames Q3's operating loss 'mainly' on higher credit impairment losses. That reverses Q2, when general-unsecured C-M3 flow fell to 1.0% from 1.2% and DPD30+ to 6.1% from 6.4%, and credit impairment was RMB4,141m (about -8% q/q). Q3 asset-quality metrics (flow rate, DPD30+/90+, risk-bearing share at 93.2%) are first disclosed in tonight's release. The net-loss range itself is already public.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 results (18 Aug 2026, 6pm ET): -5.2% next session ($15.30 to $14.50 split-adjusted, Yahoo), even though Q2 credit metrics improved. Q3 2025 business update (Oct 2025): -5.13% intraday on DPD30+ rising to 5.1% and the loan balance down 11% (https://www.itiger.com/news/1109112794). Profit warning of 16 Oct 2026: -1.8% ($8.84 to $8.68).
findings.why_not_priced: The warning gave a net-loss range and a cause but no credit metrics. The stock fell only 1.8% on it, so the market has not seen how much worse asset quality got. If the deterioration were fully priced, the warning day would not have been the smallest down day of the slide. The stock is far lower than before the warning, though, so part of it is in the price.
findings.independence: Q2 metrics come from the Q2 release (https://finviz.com/news/383498/lufax-reports-second-quarter-2026-financial-results). This shares the profit-warning document with finding 2.

findings.finding: Part of the RMB1.3-1.7bn Q3 loss is two non-cash or one-off tax charges named in the warning: (a) a reduction of deferred tax assets 'based on the company's assessment of its financing guarantee subsidiary', which implies lower expected future taxable profit there; (b) tax on planned dividends from PRC subsidiaries to offshore entities after the An Ke notes were redeemed. The print splits operating loss from tax for the first time, and Liu Jia, appointed CFO effective 16 Oct, takes his first call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior tax or DTA surprise found for this name. Management changes have moved it before: +5.14% on a new CRO appointment (Oct 2025, https://www.itiger.com/hant/news/1108052372).
findings.why_not_priced: The split between the tax charges and the operating loss is not disclosed. A large tax share would read as a cleared deck; a small one would mean an operating loss of more than RMB1bn. If the market had a view, the warning-day reaction would have been larger in one direction. The DTA write-down also signals a weaker forward outlook for the guarantee subsidiary, so the sign is ambiguous and the size small.
findings.independence: Same document as finding 1. The CFO appointment is in the same 6-K (Ex. 99.2), with coverage at https://stock.10jqka.com.cn/20261018/c680805095.shtml.

findings.finding: Cash is flowing to the parent, not funding growth. Under the 20 Aug 2026 amendment, the An Ke Technology convertible notes (US$468.9m principal, Ping An affiliate) are redeemed in two tranches in October and December 2026. Lufax also pays PAOH US$29.4m to extend its notes (US$976.9m total Ping An notes before the redemption) to 8 Oct 2027. Cash at bank was RMB19.2bn on 30 June, down from RMB22.1bn at year-end.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EGM approving the extension (8 Oct 2026): -3.47% that day per the baseline's 6-K list ($9.81 to $9.47).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the terms have been public since August. What remains is whether the Q3 balance sheet shows the first tranche and offshore cash falling more than expected. I answered the financing question: the money repays the parent and does not fund a ramp, so the sign is negative but tiny.
findings.independence: Same terms in the 6-K of 2026-08-20 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1816007/000119312526358258/d125181d6k.htm) and the 10jqka summary (https://stock.10jqka.com.cn/20261018/c680805095.shtml). It overlaps the tax item in finding 2 (the dividends upstream exist to pay this), but that finding is about the P&L charge and this one about cash.

findings.finding: Positioning has been washed out into the print. The ADS is down 33% in 20 days and 72% since January (split-adjusted from about $29 to $8.31). Market cap is about US$0.6bn (1.73bn shares, 20 per ADS) against reported net assets of RMB81.4bn (about US$11.4bn), or about 0.05x book. On 26 Oct the Hong Kong line (6623) jumped from HK$3.69 to HK$4.70 (+27%) on about 6x its recent volume, and the ADS rose 5.2% on about 2x volume. HK then fell back to about HK$3.55 on 27 Oct. I found no announcement explaining the spike.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: HK resumption news (23 Sep amc): +10.66% next day. The sell-off since then has met every piece of company news with further declines.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a statement about how much bad news is already in the price, not about the company. A sell-off this deep into a pre-announced loss leaves room for relief if credit metrics are not catastrophic. The unexplained HK spike shows someone was willing to pay up the day before the print. If the market expected a disaster, short interest would be higher than 6.5% and the warning would have moved the stock more. Ping An said in July 2024 it had no intention to take Lufax private, so I have not filed a take-private thesis.
findings.independence: ADS tape: https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/LU?range=3mo&interval=1d. Net assets from the Q2 release (https://finviz.com/news/383498/lufax-reports-second-quarter-2026-financial-results). Short interest from the MarketBeat page.

findings.finding: Ping An Bank's Q3 2026 results (released around 23-24 Oct) show personal loans of RMB1,722.5bn, -0.3% year to date and RMB4.5bn lower in the quarter, with retail credit demand still weak. Lufax's own release had described small-business financing demand as 'staying weak'. This is a weak sector proxy, not Lufax's own number.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Loan-balance declines were cited for the -5.13% intraday move on the Q3 2025 update.
findings.why_not_priced: Little: weak Chinese retail credit is a known theme, and this is a proxy from a sister company with no confirmed transmission to Lufax's new-loan volume.
findings.independence: Proxy only. Ping An Bank's own Q3 release is summarised at https://static.weeklyonstock.com/26/1024/zbf122740.html.

outside_window.finding: The second tranche of the An Ke note redemption (December 2026) and the PAOH notes' conversion window opening on 30 April 2027.

baseline_tension: The baseline has no usable options anchor. The 33% 20-day slide matches my slight negative lean on credit quality but also argues that much of it is priced, so I hold p_up near 50 (46) rather than pressing the negative.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (finding inside a company-guided range): credit-impairment finding cut from -1.0 to -0.6, because the profit warning already set the net-loss range and named the cause
Lesson 2 (one-offs as fractions): tax/DTA finding cut from -0.3 to -0.2; kept as one_off because no guide exists
Lesson 5 (unexplained moves and proxies): positioning finding cut from +1.0 to +0.7 because the HK spike has no identified cause; Ping An Bank proxy cut from -0.3 to -0.2
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): An Ke redemption checked; it repays the parent and funds no ramp, so it stays a tiny negative at -0.2
Untrustworthy-history rule: base rate rebuilt from confirmed releases; abs_move_pct kept at 7 and p_up at 46, unchanged
